question: What will happen next with respect to the 30-year U.S. Treasury yield?

calls.reasoning: As of Oct 13-14, 2026 the ^TYX close was ~5.55-5.60%, after a 52-week high close of 5.67% on Oct 7. That is ~45bp below 6.00% and ~55-60bp above 5.00%, with ~54 trading days to the end of 2026. Under a random walk at 5-7bp/day, P(touch 6.00%) is ~23-38% and P(below 5.00%) is ~14-28%. Polymarket's 30y ladders (Treasury par-yield source, a near-miss contract) price hit 6.00% at ~19% (5.90% at 24%) and below 5.00% at ~6%, on thin volume ($7-45k per strike). Trend drivers point up: Fed hiking, CPI 3.6-3.7%, Iran-war energy shock, AI bond issuance, MBS hedging. A ceasefire or growth scare is the downside path. I blend the market with the vol model and tilt slightly up from the market on both tails, since a random walk gives fatter tails than the market prices.
calls.dossier:
- 30y yield (^TYX-like) ~5.56% on Oct 13 2026 and ~5.55-5.60% on Oct 14 (macroradar; CNBC Oct 14; tradingeconomics). The 52-week range per macroradar is 4.54% (Oct 22 2025) to 5.67% (Oct 7 2026). Oct 8 was 5.60%. Herald Economy/Reuters cite 5.61% on Oct 12, a 20-year high.
- CNBC Sep 24 2026: the 30y hit its highest since 2004 amid a bond rout.
- 10y ~5.20-5.23% (Oct 14) with an intraday high ~5.34% on Oct 1; the 2y is ~4.77-4.80%. The 10s30s spread is ~37bp and steepening.
- Drivers up: Iran war since Feb 2026 (the 10y is +135bp since), a Fed hike in Sep 2026 to 3.75-4.00% with one more projected, headline CPI expected 3.6-3.7% y/y (Sep CPI released Oct 14; core ~2.4-2.5%), Goldman's estimate of $420bn of hyperscaler bond issuance next year, MBS convexity hedging, rate-options vol.
- Drivers down: war de-escalation / lower energy prices, a growth scare or equity selloff (flight to quality), soft core inflation (core is only ~2.5%).
- The next FOMC is ~late Oct/early Nov 2026, with a December FOMC also in the window.
- Human markets: Polymarket has 30y 'how high' and 'how low' before-2027 ladders. They resolve on Treasury daily par yields, not Yahoo ^TYX (a near-miss contract). Volumes are thin ($3k-45k per strike).
- Resolution: off the Yahoo Finance ^TYX daily close history; whichever threshold is crossed first after Oct 10 2026 wins. Intraday prints don't count.
- Event window: Oct 10 2026 -> Dec 31 2026 per the criteria; as of Oct 14 ~5% elapsed (~54 trading days remain).
- Distances from ~5.56%: +44bp to 6.00%, -56bp to 5.00%. Historical 30y daily vol in 2022-2026 is ~5-8bp, so a 1-sigma move over 54 days is ~37-59bp.
- Searched but not found: a Kalshi long-horizon 30y threshold contract (only daily markets) and the exact Yahoo ^TYX close series for October.
calls.reference_class: Barrier-hit probabilities for a 30y Treasury yield random walk over a ~2.5-month window at 2022-2026 realized vol (5-7bp/day), cross-checked against Polymarket 30y yield threshold ladders

A barrier model using realized vol (~44-50bp over the horizon) gives roughly 30% up and 20% down; near-miss Polymarket ladders (Treasury par-yield source, thin) imply lower vol, at ~19% for 6.00 and ~6% for below 5.00. calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the facts: last close 5.56, distances 44/56bp, ~55 trading days left, Yahoo close-only resolution, not resolved yet since Oct 10. The disputes were judgment calls: the vol regime (realized ~6bp/day vs the lower vol implied by Polymarket ladders) and how much to tilt upward. Without web access I couldn't settle the vol question. I weighted the market-implied vol a bit more because only closes count and the markets have money behind them, while keeping a realized-vol premium given the current selloff. The upside tilt is justified by momentum and the drivers. Final: 22% up / 9% down / 69% neither.
